issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies that Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns a String (and that the method should return messages like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with return type boolean and Goat/Seal implementations print the message and return true. This return-type mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students about the expected signature and return value and prevents them from implementing the interface as specified in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable interface and its implementations with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and update Goat and Seal to return the message String (e.g., "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Alternatively, if boolean is intended, update the problem statement/UML to indicate a boolean return and adjust the textual instructions to match.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (the message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with a boolean return type and implementations print the message and return true. This creates an API/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (milking an animal) and will confuse students mapping the specification to the expected implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface follow the problem specification by changing messageOnMilk() to return String and have implementations return the message (e.g., "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing it and returning boolean. Alternatively, update the problem statement to require a boolean and printed output, but keeping the interface returning String aligns better with the described behavior and expected return value.
